newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down on trade balance worries.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down on trade balance worries.

text.p: Thai stocks ended slightly lower in thin dealings on Thursday as investors sold shares due to concerns over Thailand's weak exports and unimpressive economic indicators, brokers said.

"Investors continued to sell today as they found that key economic indicators, especially exports, were not impressive. Local speculators were active in the market today," said Thanawat Patchimkul of Seamico Securities.
The composite SET index fell for the sixth consecutive trading day, dipping 1.37 points to close at 688.42 on 2.2 billion baht turnover.
The SET-50 index dropped 0.23 point to 51.89.
Gainers edged decliners 132 to 115 while 111 issues were unchanged.

The Bank of Thailand said in the afternoon that the country's exports in February narrowed to 108.6 billion baht from 115.9 billion in January. Imports in February also fell to 130.3 billion from 154.9 billion in January.

"The trade balance during the period improved simply because of the slow down in imports. Thailand's chronic economy problems remain there and that's why stock investors were disappointed," Thanawat said.
Several bouts of profit-taking were seen during the session. However, the index moved in a narrow range and brokers said the market had probably reached its bottom.

The banking sector was first-ranked in terms of value, falling 0.01 percent, followed by the communication sector which dropped 1.09 percent, and the building and materials sector which ended up 0.16 percent.
Large capitalised Bangkok Bank topped the active list, falling one baht to 185 while Siam Cement advanced four to 656 and TelecomAsia lost 0.50 to 41.
